description:
Give the two storage backends one gate-run record reader with one set of clutter and corruption rules, so the per-issue layout changes one reader.

## Background

The JSON and memory backends each implement `read_gate_runs` and `load_gate_run_result` with their own enumeration and clutter logic (`crates/jit/src/storage/json.rs`, `storage/memory.rs`). `storage/gate_runs.rs` is a test module, so the reader needs its own file. `read_repository_file_nofollow` (`storage/repository_state_store.rs`) takes a filesystem root, so the memory backend cannot sit on it, and no directory-listing primitive spans both backends; `read_path_bytes` resolves against the worktree root and goes through git2.

`test_gate_run_readers_*` in `storage/issue_store_conformance.rs` already owns the clutter, symlink and corruption rules across both backends. Paired per-backend tests re-prove them: the per-backend `test_gate_run_readers_*` in `json.rs` and `memory.rs` and the helper `gate_run_parent_entry` in `memory.rs`. `test_held_gate_run_directory_capability_cannot_escape_after_parent_symlink_swaps` in `json.rs` is file-backend behaviour and stays.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `storage/gate_run_reader.rs` holds the one reader for listing and loading gate-run records, generic over a backend seam with two methods: list the child names of one directory, and read one regular file without following a symlink. The file backend implements the seam on its no-follow primitives and the memory backend over its map. Neither backend keeps its own enumeration, clutter or parse code for run records.
- [hard] REQ-02: The `test_gate_run_readers_*` cases in `issue_store_conformance.rs` plant records through `VirtualPath::gate_run_record`, pass unchanged in what they assert, and gain any rule only a per-backend test covers.
- [hard] REQ-03: The per-backend `test_gate_run_readers_*` tests and `gate_run_parent_entry` no longer exist, and `test_held_gate_run_directory_capability_cannot_escape_after_parent_symlink_swaps` still passes.
title: Both storage backends read gate-run records through one reader
